## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded a critical deficiency in pump operation. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a failure condition requiring immediate professional attention. All other measured components are in good condition.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter was in good condition with light soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP OPERATION -- CRITICAL FINDING
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Load % | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | 22.2% | CRITICAL |

The pump motor is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated full-load amperage. This indicates the pump is operating with no hydraulic load. The motor is at risk of overheating without fluid circulation to provide cooling.

**Probable causes:**
- Impeller is broken or missing
- Discharge line is severed or disconnected
- Pump is running dry (no fluid present at the intake)

The high water alarm tested functional and electrical connections are sound, so the control circuit is intact. The failure is in the pump's ability to move fluid.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (Critical):**
- Immediate professional attention is required. A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for disconnection or damage, and must check the impeller for breakage or absence. Do not delay this service -- continued operation risks motor burnout and system failure.

**Routine:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once pump operation is restored.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure
The pump is running but not moving water. This can happen if the impeller inside the pump breaks, if the discharge line comes loose or splits, or if the pump intake is blocked. Without water flow, the motor will overheat and fail completely. This needs to be fixed right away.

### Solids Management
This maintenance visit recorded solids at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids accumulate naturally over time. Keeping non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease -- keeps that accumulation slow and predictable.
